sentences.text: Heard.

2. This is an application seeking to quash F.I.R. in Crime No.0113/2024 registered by non-applicant No.1 for the offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
3. It is the informant's case that there has been an agreement to sell in respect of sale of 50% portion of concerned land in his favour.
The said agreement dated 4.4.2015 has been executed by co-accused Rajesh Dawda and Sudhanshu Devgekar.

As regards to these applicants Mahesh Fulwani and Narendra Gandhi are concerned, it is alleged that despite knowledge of prior agreement they have entered into an agreement of the same property with vendors and thus the offence of breach of trust and cheating is committed.
4. It is applicants' contention that the agreement executed in their favour dated 10.11.2017 was well within the knowledge of the informant since beginning.
The informant himself has filed a suit for specific performance in the year 2019 against the vendor in which applicants have also been joined.
It is brought to our notice that temporary injunction application in said suit came to be rejected in the year 2021.
Likewise the non-applicant No.2 has also filed a suit in the year 2021 against co-accused (vendors) and the informant which is pending.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 5. Precisely it is their case where owner of the property (co-accused) have initially entered into agreement to sell of partial piece of land on 4.4.2015 whilst the entire land was subsequently again agreed to be sold on 10.11.2017 with applicant No.1 Mahesh Fulwani.
Both have filed civil suits against each other which demonstrate knowledge of rival agreements.

6. The applicants' learned Senior Advocate has argued that the transaction dates back to the year 2017 and on failure to secure favourable order in civil suit, belated report has been lodged with police after 6 years to settle the score.
The learned Senior Advocate would submit that prima facie ingredients to constitute the offence are not made out.
It is his contention that the matter is purely of civil nature which is coloured as a criminal prosecution to put the applicants to the knees.

7. Learned Senior Advocate Mr. Mirza made an unusual prayer to stay the proceedings by submitting that the applicants who are reputed persons of the society are being unnecessarily harassed on account of registration of crime.

To support his contention he has relied on the decisions in case of Mohammad Ibrahim and others V/s. State of Bihar and another reported in (2009) 8 SCC 751 and Neeharika Infrastructure Private Limited V/s. State of Maharashtra and others reported in (2021) 19 SCC 401 wherein it is observed that in exceptional cases, the Court can stay the investigation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is alleged that no cognizable offence is made out and the 3 apl1094.2024 prosecution is filed with ulterior motive.
8. We are satisfied about these submissions for staying the investigation as a case of exceptional nature has been made out.
9. At this juncture, learned A.P.P. has objected to stay the investigation.
10. In the canvass of above peculiar facts and considering the civil nature of the litigation, prima facie, we deem it appropriate to stay the investigation till the next date of hearing.
11. Issue notice to the non-applicants returnable on 12.9.2024.

12. Ms. M.H. Deshmukh, learned A.P.P. waives notice for non-applicant No.1.
13.
The investigation shall be stayed till next date of hearing.
(MRS.VRUSHALI V.JOSHI, J.) (VINAY JOSHI, J.) Signed by: MR. N.V.Tambaskar.
